findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice/placeholder syntax introduced into an i18next-consumed message bundle
findings.body: This file is consumed by the account console (i18next), where parameters are interpolated with the `{{n}}` syntax – every other parameterized key in this file uses it (e.g. `error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.`). The new value `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` uses Java `MessageFormat` single-brace placeholders plus a `choice` format, neither of which i18next understands. As a result the user will see the literal text `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of actual values. The previous `{{0}} ... value(s)` form worked; only the server-side (Java) bundles should use choice formats.

findings.title: Admin console message switched to Java MessageFormat syntax that i18next cannot render
findings.body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This bundle is rendered by the admin console through i18next, which interpolates `{{n}}` (see neighbouring keys such as `error-invalid-length` in the same file) and has no support for `MessageFormat` choice formats. The message will be displayed with raw `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` and the whole `{2,choice,...}` block visible to administrators.

findings.title: Diff trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException while reporting a violation
findings.body:
The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) scans are independent, so the two regions can overlap and `start + end` can exceed the length of `value` or `sanitized`. `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` then fails with StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. A concrete example: value `x

y` sanitized to `x
y` gives start=5, end=5, so `sanitized.substring(5, 1)` throws. Instead of a readable "Illegal HTML in key ..." message the plugin crashes with an unrelated runtime exception, hiding the actual problem. Clamp `end` to `min(len) - start` before building the substrings.

findings.title: Missing English reference bundle aborts the build with an opaque RuntimeException
findings.body: The English counterpart path is derived purely by string replacement (`resources-community` -> `resources`, `_<locale>.properties` -> `_en.properties`). If that file does not exist (community-only theme/locale layout, a bundle whose name does not follow the `_xx.properties` convention, or a locale containing digits which the `[a-zA-Z-_]*` class does not match), the constructor throws an unchecked RuntimeException out of `verify()`, which declares `MojoExecutionException`. The Maven run then fails with a raw stack trace rather than a diagnosable plugin error, and the file is not verified. Either skip verification when no reference bundle exists or wrap the failure in MojoExecutionException with the computed path.

findings.title: Anchor-mismatch error message does not identify the file or key
findings.body: `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` omits both the properties file and the message key, unlike the HTML message a few lines below which includes them. With hundreds of bundles verified in one build, a contributor cannot tell which translation to fix. The already-passed `key` parameter is unused; include it and `file` in the message.

findings.title: Unescaping HTML entities turns safe escaped markup into reported violations
findings.body: `normalizeValue` runs `unescapeHtml4` on the raw property value, so a translation that deliberately contains escaped markup (e.g. `<div>`) becomes real markup before sanitization. The sanitizer strips it and the key is then reported as "Illegal HTML" even though the original value is harmless literal text. This produces false positives that contributors can only work around by rewording the message.

findings.title: Verification compares sanitizer output verbatim, flagging harmless HTML formatting as illegal
findings.body:
The check requires the message to be byte-identical to the OWASP sanitizer's re-serialized output. Semantically identical markup that the sanitizer normalizes differently (for example `
` vs `
`, attribute quoting/order, or whitespace inside tags) is reported as "Illegal HTML", which is both misleading and brittle – this is why ~20 translation files in this PR had to be rewritten from `
` to `
`. Any future contribution using the other spelling will fail CI with a security-sounding error. Consider comparing the set of allowed elements/attributes, or normalizing both sides through the sanitizer before comparison.

findings.title: Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian bundle
findings.body: `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous Lithuanian sentence was replaced (presumably copied from the Italian bundle while removing the `<a href=...>` links). Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the OTP setup page. The same problem was introduced in `theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`loginTotpStep1`).

findings.title: Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian login bundle
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian text in the Lithuanian login messages. It replaces the former Lithuanian sentence, so the OTP setup screen for the `lt` locale now shows Italian.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text placed in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
findings.body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese wording/characters (手機, 應用程式) and appears to have been copied from the zh_TW bundle, while this file is zh_CN (Simplified). Simplified-Chinese users will see Traditional characters on the OTP setup page; the Simplified equivalent is e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

findings.title: No test asserting that valid messages produce no findings
findings.body: All four tests only assert that a violation is reported. Nothing verifies the negative case: that a bundle whose translation legitimately contains the allowed elements (`br`, `p`, `strong`, `b`), the same anchor as the English source, placeholders such as `{0}`/`{{0}}`, or a `{n,choice,...}` block yields an empty message list. Given how much special-casing `normalizeValue`/`santizeAnchors` contain, false positives (which would break the whole themes build) are the most likely regression and are currently untested.
